This vignette gives the design of the simulation study in the paper, the code
that runs it, and its main results. The code is not run when the vignette is
built: the study takes about 80 minutes on six cores. The results below were
produced with the development version that became 0.1.0; version 0.1.0
reproduces them exactly.

```{r setup}
library(cortisol.nmea)
```

## Design

Each trimester has ten independent cohorts of 100 people, generated from the
package's built-in references. Every cohort is analysed without contamination
(D0), with mild contamination (D1: 5% of samples raised by 4-8 noise SDs) and
with strong contamination (D2: 10% raised by 8-12 noise SDs). The three
scenarios of a cohort share its people, sampling times and clean noise.

Five methods are fitted. Direct NMEA, Full NMEA (the default workflow) and the
GAMM comparator are the main comparison. Full NMEA with the original fixed
cutoff of 6 nmol/L and with a MAD-based cutoff are supplementary arms for the
choice of the outlier rule.

```{r design}
ctrl <- nmea_control()   # 300 + 100 SAEM iterations, seed 632545
methods <- list(
  Direct = method_nmea(nmea_steps_direct(), ctrl),
  Full = method_nmea(nmea_steps(), ctrl),                               # default rule
  Full_fixed6 = method_nmea(nmea_steps(outlier = outlier_fixed(6)), ctrl),
  Full_MAD = method_nmea(nmea_steps(outlier = outlier_sd(2.75, "mad")), ctrl),
  GAMM = method_gamm()
)
design <- sim_design(
  trimesters = c("T1", "T2", "T3"), n = 100,
  seeds = list(T1 = 610161001:610161010, T2 = 610162001:610162010, T3 = 610163001:610163010),
  scenarios = c("D0", "D1", "D2"), methods = methods
)
```

## Running

```{r run}
future::plan(future::multisession, workers = 6)
runs <- sim_run(design, cache_dir = "paper-simulation-cache", parallel = TRUE)
saveRDS(runs, "paper-simulation-runs.rds")
```

## Tables and figures

```{r tables}
main <- c("Direct", "Full", "GAMM")
eval_summary(runs, methods = main)$summary
eval_paired(runs, "Full", "Direct")$summary
eval_paired(runs, "Full", "GAMM")$summary
eval_paired(runs, "Full", "Full_fixed6")$summary
eval_paired(runs, "Full", "Full_MAD")$summary
eval_retention(runs, "Full")$summary
eval_detection(runs, "Full")$summary
```

Figure 1 shows one third-trimester cohort under the three scenarios and four
example people. The examples were chosen by rules fixed before the study was
run: in D2, the first person whose contaminated samples were all removed and no
clean sample was (S0001), and the first whose detection was incomplete
(S0002); in D0, the person whose Full NMEA error was closest to the cohort
median (S0085); and in D2, the first person without contamination who lost a
clean sample (S0028).

```{r figures}
plot_cohort_curves(runs, "T3", seed = 610163001, methods = main)
for (ex in list(c("T3_S0001", "D2"), c("T3_S0002", "D2"), c("T3_S0085", "D0"), c("T3_S0028", "D2"))) {
  print(plot_subject(runs, ex[1], trimester = "T3", seed = 610163001, scenario = ex[2], methods = main))
}
plot_recovery(runs, "rmse", methods = main)
plot_recovery(runs, "auc_error", methods = main)
plot_detection(runs, "Full", "D2")
plot_retention(runs, "Full", "D2")
sim_report(runs, "paper-simulation-report.html", methods = main)
```

The report uses the same three methods as the main tables, so its common
subjects match them. A report over all five methods
(`sim_report(runs, "all-methods.html")`) uses a different (usually smaller) set
of common subjects and should be labelled as such.

## Results

Of 450 method fits, one failed: the GAMM fit of one second-trimester cohort
without contamination (a singular matrix). It was kept as a failure. Comparisons
involving GAMM in D0 therefore use 29 of 30 cohorts and are marked incomplete;
they describe the valid cohorts only.

Curve RMSE (nmol/L) on the people all three main methods could fit, with 95%
Monte Carlo intervals; trimesters weighted equally:

| Scenario | Direct | Full | GAMM |
|---|---|---|---|
| D0 (29/30) | 0.877 [0.851, 0.904] | 0.896 [0.870, 0.922] | 1.597 [1.561, 1.633] |
| D1 | 1.212 [1.169, 1.255] | 1.090 [1.051, 1.129] | 1.821 [1.781, 1.862] |
| D2 | 2.374 [2.264, 2.485] | 1.342 [1.276, 1.408] | 2.397 [2.311, 2.482] |

Paired differences, Full minus comparator, on the people both methods could
fit (negative favours Full):

| Comparison | D0 | D1 | D2 |
|---|---|---|---|
| Full - Direct | +0.018 [-0.010, 0.046] | -0.122 [-0.181, -0.063] | -1.032 [-1.169, -0.896] |
| Full - GAMM | -0.701 [-0.739, -0.663] | -0.731 [-0.779, -0.683] | -1.055 [-1.159, -0.950] |

Without contamination the two NMEA fits are equivalent. With contamination the
full workflow recovers curves better, and under strong contamination it was
better than both comparators in all 30 cohorts. These errors are for retained
people: under strong contamination Full NMEA kept 93.1%, 89.8% and 88.3% of
people in the three trimesters.

Against the fixed cutoff of 6 nmol/L, the default rule gave the same accuracy
(D2 RMSE difference +0.010 [-0.030, 0.050]; D1 +0.021 [0.005, 0.038]) but more
even detection across trimesters: under strong contamination it removed 5.7%,
4.5% and 5.1% of clean samples, against 1.9%, 5.3% and 9.3%, and kept 4.4
percentage points more people in the third trimester. The MAD-based cutoff
removed 2.6-5.2% of clean samples without contamination, with larger curve
errors (D0 RMSE difference -0.051 [-0.077, -0.025] in favour of the default),
and no gain under contamination.
